messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — autoscaler ceiling hit in eu-west-1 for nodepool `gpu-prod-eu`. backpressure detected: request queue length > 1200, throttling, multiple 5xxs. paging maya (oncall) :rotating_light:
maya (oncall): on it. confirming scope and impact. runbook link?
adrian (infra): runbook: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/autoscale-ceiling. quick check: cluster shows nodepool `gpu-prod-eu` at maxNodes=12 and ASG/quota at 12/12. no further scale possible.
kevin (mlops): we're seeing inference queue backlog on the redis queue and per-replica token-serving rate dropping. some long-running jobs are pinning GPUs (kv cache warm).
amber (support): CS: two enterprise customers reporting 503s and timeouts for embedding/finetune endpoints. ticket #CS-4982 and #CS-4983. they're asking ETA.
maya (oncall): ok — immediate triage plan: 1) short-term relief: add temporary burst pool or evict non-prod pods 2) medium: request manual cap raise / quota increase 3) long-term: improve packable scheduling. who's ok to do the hotpatch?
adrian (infra): I can run a manual nodepool add but need infra-admin consent for service-account escalation (TFC policy). alternatives: we can enable eviction of preemptible-test workloads on the cluster to free ~2 nodes.
kevin (mlops): evicting test jobs will help but some prod jobs are long-lived. could we create a CPU-backend fallback pool for light-weight routing for non-critical requests? config change ok but needs quick routing rule.
maya (oncall): amber, please confirm which customers impacted so we can message. eloise, can you draft a short PSAT?
eloise (customer-success): drafting now: "We're aware of degraded performance for embeddings & generation; engineering is actively mitigating; next update in 30m." will post after you approve.
amber (support): affected: acme-inc (high priority) and datumai. both showing spikes starting 09:12UTC.
adrian (infra): quick status checks:
```
# kubectl get nodepool gpu-prod-eu -o yaml | egrep 'name|maxNodes|ready'
name: gpu-prod-eu
maxNodes: 12
readyNodes: 12
```
and cloud quota: GPUs allocated 12/12 in eu-west-1.
maya (oncall): last resort: I can request manual cap +3 for this nodepool from infra leads. can someone approve now? need rapid decision since queue still rising. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
adrian (infra): I'm offline from infra-admin but can approve if ops-manager gives verbal ok. tagging adrian (infra) — (he/him) — can we get a rapid approval?
kevin (mlops): small mitigation we can do now: change podPriority of non-customer jobs to low and set `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` on test nodes to reclaim ~1-2 GPUs. i'll prepare pod selectors.
maya (oncall): do it. kevin, proceed with eviction now. amber, please set customer comms to "engineering working mitigation, ETA 20-30m"
kevin (mlops): running:
```
kubectl get pods -n default -o wide | grep test | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r kubectl delete pod --grace-period=5
```
kevin (mlops): deleted ~18 test pods, reclaiming 1 node worth of capacity. queue length down to ~900 now.
amber (support): PSAT message posted to customers.
deploy-bot: terraform run queued for infra-change: update nodepool `gpu-prod-eu` maxNodes 15 (pending manual approval). Initiated by maya.
maya (oncall): requesting manual cap raise +3. adrian — can you authorise terraform apply? we need to lift limit to 15 for now.
adrian (infra): I can approve. i'm elevating the TFC run. giving go for manual apply. tag: @infra-admins for audit.
adrian (infra): terraform plan snippet:
```
resource "gke_node_pool" "gpu_prod_eu" {
  name       = "gpu-prod-eu"
  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 6
    max_node_count = 15  # bumped from 12
  }
}
```
maya (oncall): maya executing the plan now. will monitor.
deploy-bot: terraform apply started by maya (oncall). plan id: tf-2026-07-12-001
adrian (infra): note: we still need cloud quota increase after this; this is temporary — we'll request quota through support ticket with cloud.
kevin (mlops): while apply runs, I'm also flipping scheduler packing: set `scheduling.kubelet.eviction-threshold` lower for low-priority to free extra memory. small tweak deployed.
maya (oncall): terraform apply done. new maxNodes=15 acknowledged by cluster autoscaler. nodepool is provisioning 3 nodes (pending).
ops-bot: NODEPROV EVENT — 3 nodes provisioned in eu-west-1, node labels: gpu=true, taint: gpu=reserved:NoSchedule.
kevin (mlops): new nodes joined, pods are draining backlog. queue length down to 120, per-replica throughput up.
amber (support): customers reporting improvement, acme-inc says success; closing CS-4982 with note.
eloise (customer-success): sending follow-up message: "All systems recovering; teams will follow up with detailed postmortem and remediation steps."
adrian (infra): filing a follow-up for quota request and runbook update (we need a documented hotpath for temporary nodepool creation that bypasses TFC approval in emergencies).
maya (oncall): summary: immediate: evicted test pods + manual nodepool bump + small scheduler tweak. impact: short degradation for two customers, now resolved. actions: 1) open cloud quota ticket 2) update runbook with explicit emergency step + owner 3) schedule postmortem tomorrow 10:00UTC.
maya (oncall): closing the incident thread — will post the postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
